## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, gaunt, and thin woman characterized by a sharp, angular frame without curves. Her dark hair, which is streaked with gray, is kept twisted behind her head in a tight little knot secured by two wire hairpins. Though described as a dark and homely child in her youth, her grayer hair and angular figure later accompany a noticeably softer face.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P44](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0044), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P15](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0015)_

## Personality

A woman of narrow experience, Marilla Cuthbert is defined by her rigid conscience, stoic demeanor, and sensible, self-contained nature. She approaches life with a sober, unromantic perspective, rarely allowing herself to be moved by sentiment or poetry. Characterized by a strict and critical attitude, she is known for her firm determination once her mind is made up, as well as her customary calm placidity. Driven by a strong sense of duty, she aims to drill [Anne](../character/anne.md) into a tranquil uniformity of disposition. Additionally, she is celebrated in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) for her skill in making three-year-old homemade currant wine.

## History

Marilla Cuthbert grew up as a dark, homely child who always obeyed orders, and she was already an adult when her family's house at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) was built. Having inherited an amethyst brooch from her mother and quarreled with her former suitor John Blythe in her youth, she lived at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) for decades alongside her brother [Matthew](../character/matthew.md). After forty-five years as neighbors with [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md), Marilla agreed to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, only to be shocked when a young girl named [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) arrived instead. Though initially determined to send the child back, Marilla took pity on Anne's tragic background and decided to raise her, focusing on the girl's proper upbringing, moral education, and practical skills. Over time, Marilla grew deeply attached to [Anne](../character/anne.md), enduring the girl's imaginative blunders with an amethyst brooch and liniment-flavored cake, while experiencing a profound realization of her love when [Anne](../character/anne.md) broke her ankle. When [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) suddenly died following a bank failure, a grief-stricken Marilla learned from an oculist that her failing eyesight threatened to force the sale of [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). However, [Anne](../character/anne.md) sacrificed her college scholarship to remain home as the local teacher, prompting Marilla to open up about her past relationship with John Blythe as they maintained the farm together. Marilla later agreed to take in her late cousin's orphaned twins, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) and [Dora](../character/dora.md), and she eventually invited the widowed [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) to live with them at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) so that [Anne](../character/anne.md) could finally attend [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college).

## Quotes

> "Well now, yes. It always kind of gives me a thrill to see them ugly white grubs that spade up in the cucumber beds. I hate the look of them."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised P58](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0058)

> "It’s five miles; and as you’re evidently bent on talking you might as well talk to some purpose by telling me what you know about yourself."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P8](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0008)

> "No, I don’t want any of your imaginings. Just you stick to bald facts. Begin at the beginning. Where were you born and how old are you?"
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P10](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0010)

> "We’re not talking about poetry, Anne—we are talking about saying your prayers. Don’t you know it’s a terrible wicked thing not to say your prayers every night? I’m afraid you are a very bad little girl."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VII. Anne Says Her Prayers P11](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0011)

> "Well, you’ll have to do without your thrill. I hadn’t any material to waste on puffed sleeves. I think they are ridiculous-looking things anyhow. I prefer the plain, sensible ones."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XI. Anne’s Impressions of Sunday-school P10](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0010)

## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla initially takes [Anne](../character/anne.md) in by mistake after requesting an orphan boy, but soon decides to keep her and becomes her mentor and adoptive mother. Though Marilla frequently commands [Anne](../character/anne.md), instructs her in domestic skills like cooking, and disciplines her dramatic outbursts, she develops a deep affection for the girl. Over time, their dynamic evolves into a warm parent-child bond as Marilla guides [Anne](../character/anne.md) through her youth.

- Commands — guardian ordering her to her room  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P22](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0022), [v2 XII A Jonah Day P35](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0035)</sub>
- Mentor of — teaching her to cook  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XVI. Diana Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results P27](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0027)</sub>
- Parent of — adoptive mother (since v2)  <sub>[v2 X Davy in Search of a Sensation P81](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0081)</sub>
